title: Hosted GPU pool queue decompression and scalability hardening
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary: During a multi-hour capacity event on 2026-03-03 the hosted API observed rapid queue buildup against several GPU pools which led to increased tail latency, degraded streaming responses, and progressive request throttling for bursty customers. This ticket tracks actionable follow-ups from the postmortem and implements resilient admission + scaling behavior to reduce future surface area for GPU exhaustion.

Incident highlight: an unexpected burst from two high-throughput customers plus a regression in request batching logic produced a step-change in pending request counts. The autoscaler reacted but the combination of admission hysteresis absence and cold pool spin-up latency caused queue amplification: long queues delayed throughput recovery, leading to cascaded preemption and more pressure on remaining pools.

Goals:
- Stop queue amplification early via smarter admission controls (hysteresis + per-pool soft caps).
- Reduce time-to-capacity by preemptive pool priming when predictive signals trigger.
- Ensure graceful degradation for low-priority traffic (fast-fail / rate-limited paths) to protect high-priority SLAs.
- Add observability and deterministic test coverage for queue dynamics and autoscaler behavior.

Root causes identified:
- Autoscaler threshold tuned only on GPU utilization, not on pending-queue growth (missed early signal).
- No admission hysteresis; admission gates oscillated between open/closed causing bursts to re-enter after transient drop.
- Cold-start latency for new worker pods in some regions (image cache misses) increased recovery time.
- A batching regression increased per-request GPU occupancy under a narrow sequence-length distribution.

Immediate mitigations (already applied):
1) Short-term soft admission: introduced a global emergency gate that fast-fails non-privileged requests when pending-queue > 10k (temp threshold). (owner: SRE team)
2) Raised autoscaler upper-bound temporarily to buy capacity while long-term fixes land.
3) Hotfix to revert the batching regression (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1442).

Planned action items (this ticket):
A. Admission hysteresis and per-customer priority buckets (owner: Miguel) — implement a two-stage admission gate: soft-accept until queue hits soft_cap, then apply slow-path (rate-limit token-bucket) until queue drops below soft_cap - hysteresis_margin. Include an emergency hard-fail tier for third-party traffic. Estimate: 5 pts. Target: runtime-1.20.
B. Queue-aware autoscaler hooks (owner: Priya Shah) — add pending_request_count and pending_age_p50/p95 as signals to the autoscaler decision process, with configurable weight. Include unit tests and canary rollout. Estimate: 3 pts. Target: runtime-1.20.
C. Pool priming automation (owner: Platform Infra) — predictive priming: if predictive model (short-term forecast of request rate) crosses threshold, spin warm nodes ahead of demand; fallback to region-specific warm images to cut cold-start times. Integrate with cost controls. Estimate: 5 pts. Target: runtime-1.21.
D. Fast-fail path and SLA routing (owner: API team) — add explicit fast-fail response for requests flagged low-priority with 429+Retry-After, and route critical customers to reserved capacity when configured. Estimate: 3 pts. Target: console-2026.03.
E. Observability and synthetic tests (owner: Observability) — add new dashboard panels: pending-queue flux, admission gate state, per-pool spin-up latency; create chaos test that simulates burst+regression scenarios against staging. Estimate: 2 pts. Target: runtime-1.20.

Acceptance criteria:
- Autoscaler uses queue signals in canary region and does not regress cost (validated against historical traces).
- Admission hysteresis prevents queue amplification in controlled load tests (loadtest scenarios A/B).
- Cold-start median spin-up time reduced by >=30% in priming path.
- Low-priority fast-fail responses reduce tail latency for premium customers during burst scenarios in testbed.
- Documentation and runbook updated with new thresholds, playbooks, and rollback steps.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge guarded feature flags for admission hysteresis and autoscaler queue signals behind runtime feature flags and a console toggle.
2) Canary to non-prod then to us-east-1 small pool. Observe for 48h.
3) Expand to other regions progressively and monitor cost/latency delta.
4) If regressions observed, auto-roll back via feature flag.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Overly aggressive priming increases spend and can cause wasted capacity; mitigate with success metrics and budget soft-limits.
- Incorrect hysteresis tuning may increase latency for admitted requests; mitigate with staged rollout and real-time dashboards.
- Complexity added to autoscaler could cause maintenance burden; keep config defaults conservative and document.

Documentation links and artifacts:
- Incident Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C01234INCIDENTS/p1677530000000
- Postmortem draft: https://docs.redwood.com/postmortems/2026-03-03-gpu-exhaustion
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1442
- Autoscaler proposal doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/queue-aware-autoscaler-proposal
- Synthetic loadtest harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtests/tree/queue-hysteresis

Notes: Owners should keep updates in this ticket. If any blocker emerges (security or infra quota), tag the ticket and mark status Blocked and escalate to SOC oncall.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem review. Captured immediate mitigations and prioritized hysteresis + autoscaler changes.
2026-03-06 - Miguel Alvarez: Drafted design for admission hysteresis and priority buckets. Working on API surface for token-bucket slow-path. See design sketch in Confluence.
2026-03-08 - Priya Shah: Added autoscaler signal proposal; will prototype using pending_request_count + pending_age metric. Running historical replay tests against last 6 months of traces.
2026-03-09 - SRE: Emergency soft gate applied and autoscaler upper-bound increased; saw immediate reduction in tail latency. Monitoring continues.
2026-03-11 - Miguel Alvarez: Initial implementation ready behind feature flag. Integration tests passing. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1458
2026-03-12 - QA: Synthetic burst test executed in staging with hysteresis=500/100 margin; queue stayed bounded and premium-customer latencies held. Draft test report attached to ticket.
